findings.desc: DONE-required timeout classification is not implemented across the promised layers. `runDoneRequiredValidation` records a command timeout as a FAIL receipt, but `handlers/done-required-validation.ts` maps every non-PASS to result=failed and always emits timeoutLayer=null; `done_prepare` then parses that as failed and omits timeoutLayer. The CLI idle/max watchdog in `cli-engine.ts` still calls process.exit(2), so direct/done_prepare JSON receives no terminal result at all for idle/max expiry. Even successful done_prepare reused/executed output omits timeoutLayer=null because `donePrepareJsonResult` only adds a recognized non-null token. This contradicts CHK-001/003 requirements for result=timed_out and timeoutLayer=command|phase|idle|max, and leaves the JSON contract unable to distinguish timeout from validation failure.
findings.resolvedReason: Repro: real subprocess matrices force command, phase, CLI idle, and CLI max expiry and inspect JSON plus shell status. Root cause: command receipts collapsed timeout into generic failure, done_prepare omitted routine watchdog attribution, and cli-engine force-exited before handlers could settle. Fix: timeout receipts now map to result=timed_out/timeoutLayer=command; AbortController-backed structured watchdogs propagate idle|max to direct validation and done_prepare; phase remains phase-attributed; structured failed/timed_out/blocked output stays parseable and exits nonzero. ReproTest: npm --prefix packages/main run build; node packages/main/dist/tasks/validate-progress-heartbeat-smoke.js; node packages/main/dist/tasks/done-prepare-closure-heartbeat-smoke.js. Both smoke commands PASS at HEAD a6cefb0 and assert nonzero timeout status plus immediate rerun cleanup.

findings.desc: The trusted metadata-only reuse lineage checks only the net tree diff (`git diff --name-only evidenceHead..currentHead`), not paths touched by every intervening commit. A descendant history can modify a code/config path and later restore it; that path disappears from the net diff, so this function can classify the lineage as trusted-story-metadata-descendant. This violates the documented and CHK-002 requirement that every intervening changed path be trusted metadata and that any intervening code/config path refuse reuse. Enumerate changed paths per commit across the ancestry range (including deletes/renames) or explicitly narrow the contract to final-tree equivalence.

All 28 must intents are marked covered by four smoke commands, but the assertions exercise only a small subset. Budget tests use one 1,200,000ms command: no 290,000+1,200,000 sequence, default-timeout command, malformed/non-positive inputs, unrelated CLI max, LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS, or phase/max race; phase-timeout JSON does not assert disposition/result/refusalReasons/timeoutLayer. Reuse tests call the evaluator only and never exercise done_prepare default reuse, reuseFreshDoneRequired=false, fresh/stale/missing validate=false immutability, structured failure/timeout/block outputs, malformed/unreadable evidence, full lineage matrix, or TOCTOU. Direct-handler tests run an instant child and synchronous throwing sink only: no silent heartbeat past idle, real direct CLI watchdog, explicit idle/max, passing and failing rejected sinks, boundary ordering, descendant cleanup, lock reacquisition, or late-heartbeat race. Add table-driven budget tests and hermetic real-CLI fixtures per omitted intent, then bind each evidence ref to assertions that actually exist.

Malformed or unreadable existing done-required evidence aborts the recovery path instead of being classified stale and replaced. evaluateDoneRequiredPreRunReuse calls evaluateDoneRequiredEvidence without a containment boundary (done-prepare-validation-reuse.ts:97), while StoryStore deliberately rethrows JSON parse/read errors for this artifact (store.ts:236-241). Both direct done_required_validate (done-required-validation.ts:46) and done_prepare validate=false/validate=true invoke that evaluator before they can execute or report structured status. A truncated JSON file therefore throws out of the command; even a valid JSON object with missing arrays can trigger TypeErrors in the canonical evaluator. This violates the fail-closed-but-convergent contract: malformed evidence must yield existingEvidenceBasis=stale with a refusal reason, validate=false must remain observation-only, and validate=true/direct validation must be able to run once and overwrite bad evidence. Catch artifact/evaluator shape/read failures in the pre-run reuse wrapper, return reusable=false/stale with a stable malformed-or-unreadable reason, and ensure execution does not depend on parsing prior evidence.
